idea.caption: Imagine they skips their move. It is your turn again, and the arrow shows what you would play.
You take the bishop on c4 with the pawn. It attacks their queen on b3.

plies.caption: You move the pawn to b5. It attacks their bishop on c4. This leaves itself hanging (it can be taken for free or for profit).
They take the pawn on b5 with the bishop. Their bishop on c4 moved away first, so d5 is no longer possible.

extra.caption: You move the rook to b8. It pins their bishop on b5 to the queen on b3.
They move the queen to a4.
You move the bishop to b6. It pins their pawn on f2 to the king.
They move the knight to d2.
You move the pawn to a6. It attacks their bishop on b5. This leaves itself hanging (it can be taken for free or for profit).
They move the bishop to c4.
They move the knight to e4.
You move the pawn to d5. A fork: the pawn attacks their bishop on c4 and knight on e4 at once.
They take the pawn on d6 with the pawn. It attacks your knight on e7.

plies.caption: You move the pawn to d5. It attacks their bishop on c4. This leaves itself hanging (it can be taken for free or for profit).
They take the pawn on d6 with the pawn. Your knight on e7 is trapped: every square it can reach loses it.
You take the pawn on d6 with the pawn.
They move the rook to e3. It pins your knight on e7 to the king.

extra.caption: They take the pawn on d3 with the bishop. A skewer: your queen on g6 must move and the pawn on h7 behind it falls.
You move the queen to h6.
They move the knight to d2.
You move the bishop to e6. A skewer: their queen on b3 must move and the pawn on a2 behind it falls. The bishop stops guarding your pawn on b7, which is now hanging.
They move the queen to c2.
You move the knight to d5. It attacks their rook on e3.
They move the rook to e4.

card.summary: b5 lets them win material: with their best replies you lose 1 point. d5 keeps material level. Several moves held here (d5, O-O or d6); b5 was not one of them.

reasons.lost: b5 left itself hanging, and they take it.
reasons.gaveUp: The idea: d5 threatens dxc4 (winning the bishop on c4). No material changes hands within the line; the engine still rates it +0.8 for you here against -0.8 after your move, so the edge is in the position.
reasons.gone: Their bishop on c4 moved away first, so d5 is no longer possible.
